F1.title: Python Programs
F1.summary: A program is an ordered list of instructions executed from top to bottom.
F1.exampleCaption: Sending one command to the Beacon Terminal.
F1.inWorldNote: The Beacon Terminal only responds to Architects' Python instructions.

F2.title: The print() Command
F2.summary: print() shows text or numbers in the console. You can separate multiple values with commas.
F2.exampleCaption: Each print() restores part of NEO's voice.
F2.inWorldNote: Your message appears on the Beacon screen.

F3.title: Quoted Text (Strings)
F3.summary: Quotes "..." tell Python a value is text, not a command. "5" is text while 5 is a number.
F3.exampleCaption: Strings join together; integers add numerically.
F3.inWorldNote: Used to write messages onto wooden signboards.

F4.title: Comments (#)
F4.summary: Python ignores everything after # on a line. Use comments for notes or to disable faulty lines.
F4.exampleCaption: Lines starting with # do not execute.
F4.inWorldNote: Silences faulty red-alarm prints at Beacon Point.

F5.title: Escape Characters (\n, \t, \")
F5.summary: A backslash \ gives the next character a special role: \n for newline, \t for tab, \" for an inner quote.

F6.title: Reading Input with input()
F6.summary: input() waits for a user answer and always returns it as a string (str).
F6.exampleCaption: Stores the answer inside a variable.
F6.inWorldNote: The Beacon asks your name and carves it into stone.

F7.title: Order & Indentation
F7.summary: Python executes top to bottom. Leading spaces (4 spaces) group statements inside a block.
F7.exampleCaption: 4 spaces mark lines inside the block.
F7.inWorldNote: NEO's boot sequence and robot blocks depend on exact order and indentation.

F8.title: Reading Error Messages
F8.summary: Errors tell you the exact line and reason Python got stuck. NEO translates machine errors into clear hints.
F8.exampleCode: # pritn("hi") -> NameError: did you mean print?
F8.exampleCaption: Check the highlighted line number first.
F8.inWorldNote: Every machine points to what needs fixing.

V1.title: Variables (Labeled Boxes)
V1.summary: Variables store values under a name using =. You can read and reassign them later.
V1.exampleCaption: The value in 'wood' updates from 4 to 6.
V1.inWorldNote: The Variables Panel tracks updates live during replay.

D2.title: Integers (int)
D2.summary: int values are whole numbers without decimals, used for counting steps or blocks.
D2.exampleCaption: Passes an integer variable to robot.move().
D2.inWorldNote: BIT drives forward by that exact whole count.

D3.title: Decimals (float)
D3.summary: float values include a decimal point (like 1.5) for weights and continuous measurements.
D3.inWorldNote: Computes total plank weight for the Supply Grove bridge.

D5.title: Booleans (True / False)
D5.summary: bool has only two values: True or False, always capitalized.
D5.exampleCaption: True when the tile ahead is clear to cross.
D5.inWorldNote: False before building the bridge, True afterward.

D6.title: Type Conversion with int()
D6.summary: Results from scan() or input() are text (str). Convert numeric text with int(text) before doing math.
D6.inWorldNote: Fixes TypeError when adding to scanned crate labels.

T1_ARITH.title: Micro-Card: + and * Operators
T1_ARITH.summary: With numbers, + adds and * multiplies. You will explore the full operator toolkit in Arithmetic Mines!
T1_ARITH.exampleCaption: + adds numbers; * multiplies bridge length by plank weight.
T1_ARITH.inWorldNote: Introduced briefly in Supply Grove for label totals and bridge weight.

O5.title: Comparison Operators
O5.summary: Use ==, !=, >, <, >=, <= to compare two values and obtain True or False.
O5.inWorldNote: Gatehouse rune pillars glow green for True.

B1.title: Comparison to Boolean
B1.summary: Each comparison asks a yes/no question that Python answers with True or False.
B1.exampleCaption: Comparisons can be printed or placed in if headers.
B1.inWorldNote: Solves Old Tamo's four rune riddles.

B2.title: if Statement
B2.summary: if runs an indented block (4 spaces) only when its condition is True. End the header with :.
B2.exampleCaption: gate.open() executes only when color is "blue".
B2.inWorldNote: The gate opens solely for blue crystals.

B3.title: else Branch
B3.summary: else runs automatically whenever the if condition above it is False.
B3.inWorldNote: Turns on the red warning lamp.

B4.title: elif Multi-Branch
B4.summary: elif checks extra conditions in order from top to bottom. Only the first matching branch runs.
B4.exampleCaption: Three crystal colors, three distinct responses.
B4.inWorldNote: Controls gate lamps for blue, green, and other crystals.

B5.title: Logical and
B5.summary: A and B is True only when both A and B are True.
B5.exampleCaption: Requires both blue crystal AND weight >= 2.

B6.title: Logical or
B6.summary: A or B is True when at least one side is True.

B7.title: Logical not
B7.summary: not flips True to False and False to True.

L1.title: for Loops & range()
L1.summary: for repeats an indented block for each number in range(). range(6) gives 0..5; range(1, 6) gives 1..5.

L3.title: while Loops
L3.summary: while repeats as long as the condition stays True. Move or update state so the loop terminates.
L3.exampleCaption: Ideal when row length varies across scenarios.

L5.title: Skipping Steps with continue
L5.summary: continue jumps straight to the next iteration without executing remaining lines in this pass.
L5.inWorldNote: Bonus challenge on rocky farm rows.

L6.title: Nested Loops (2D Grids)
L6.summary: Outer loop steps over farm.rows; inner loop steps over farm.cols.
L6.inWorldNote: Restores the Terrace Farm waterfall and lift.

N1.title: Defining Functions (def)
N1.summary: def stores a reusable recipe. Defining a function does not run it until you call it with ().
N1.exampleCaption: Write once, call as often as needed.
N1.inWorldNote: Builds watchtower pillars in BOLT's Workshop.

N2.title: Function Parameters
N2.summary: Parameters inside def (...) receive arguments so one function handles multiple sizes.
N2.exampleCaption: build_pillar(2) and build_pillar(4) reuse the same recipe.

N3.title: Default Parameters
N3.summary: A default parameter (=3) is used whenever the caller omits that argument.

N4.title: Return Values (return)
N4.summary: return sends a computed value back to the caller. Unlike print(), it does not just display text.
N4.inWorldNote: Printing instead of returning sends None to the depot!
